GOV.rationale: Repeated contradictory disclosures, large related deposits and new related-party land spending create stewardship/opacity concerns. No proven fraud, diversion, unfair valuation or minority expropriation supports a severe integrity finding. A 4 reflects evidenced concerns without imposing the GOV≤3 override.
GOV.missing_or_limiting_evidence: Reconciled audit corrections, land valuation/title, deposit terms, recipient and economics of strategic investment.
GOV.counterevidence: Unmodified main/IFC opinions, related-party approvals asserted and full issuer price-query reply preserved.
GOV.score_basis: v 3.0 canonical factor anchors; no neutral imputation

MOAT.rationale: One disclosed Goa resort and mixed owned/leased rooms lack demonstrated brand, switching-cost or structural cost advantage. Historical intermediary management access is not proprietary demand. Location is useful but contestable.
MOAT.missing_or_limiting_evidence: Current keys, repeat/direct booking mix, ADR premium, occupancy resilience, contract exclusivity and contribution economics.
MOAT.counterevidence: Owned premises and a long operating history provide a tangible operating base; not every small hotel lacks local appeal.
MOAT.score_basis: v 3.0 canonical factor anchors; no neutral imputation

REV.rationale: Window chosen before scoring: FY2021 is a pandemic closure trough, so use the three-year FY23–FY26 comparable reported revenue CAGR of -5.27%, starting score 1, net adjustment 0. FY26 room+F&B revenue declined 1.67% and other operating revenue drives reported growth; no sustained evidence supports a trajectory upgrade.
REV.missing_or_limiting_evidence: Disaggregated other operating income and current room/yield/volume bridge; no acquired growth is assumed.
REV.counterevidence: FY26 total revenue grew 23.16%; five-year trough-based CAGR is 18.48%, disclosed but not opportunistically scored.
REV.score_basis: v 3.0 canonical factor anchors; no neutral imputation

DUR.rationale: Leisure demand and an existing resort offer continuing business, but access to new growth is constrained by single-property concentration, lease uncertainty and unverified land/strategic project execution. Proposed diversified objects do not establish accessible profitable demand.
DUR.missing_or_limiting_evidence: Current operating agreements, permits, construction/key pipeline, realistic ramp and contracted demand.
DUR.counterevidence: Goa tourism and renewed rooms could support recovery; peer disclosures show that hotel demand exists, not that Mac will capture it.
DUR.score_basis: v 3.0 canonical factor anchors; no neutral imputation

CAP.rationale: No attributable incremental refurbishment/room cohort returns or valid comparable aggregate reinvestment bridge is established. Current/aggregate ROCE and an approximately 0.98% unadjusted incremental proxy are diagnostics, not a substitute for verified incremental project economics.
CAP.missing_or_limiting_evidence: Maintenance versus expansion split, project in-service dates, occupied-room yields, recurring contribution and related-deposit/land/investment returns.
CAP.counterevidence: Positive EBITDA and tangible investment may eventually produce returns. Unknown return attribution is not automatically a low score.
CAP.score_basis: v 3.0 canonical factor anchors; no neutral imputation

CASH.rationale: Two years of large negative CFO persist after reversing deposit additions and the debt-maturity classification. FY24–26 cumulative CFO is negative 6.163 crore against positive PAT 0.929 crore. Large aged/disputed receivables and payer/deposit concentration undermine realization.
CASH.missing_or_limiting_evidence: Recovery of old claims, deposit cash terms, and classification-corrected issuer cash-flow reconciliation.
CASH.counterevidence: Cash conversion was positive in FY23–24 and deposits are investments rather than all lost revenue; even generous deposit addbacks leave negative FY25–26 operating cash. Persistent weakness triggers GQS ceiling 5 if otherwise computable.
CASH.score_basis: v 3.0 canonical factor anchors; no neutral imputation

BAL.rationale: March cash 0.467 crore versus gross debt 5.145 crore, heavy subsequent programme cash use and optional future warrant exercise indicate fragile funding resilience. This is a balance-sheet weakness supported by dated facts, not a claim of demonstrated default.
BAL.missing_or_limiting_evidence: Recent published unrestricted cash, debt changes, essential programme obligations, deferrability, lease/statutory liabilities and committed funding.
BAL.counterevidence: May financing did deliver 8.429 crore cash and bank maturities are mostly long dated; CARO reports no default.
BAL.score_basis: v 3.0 canonical factor anchors; no neutral imputation

EXEC.rationale: Financing and refurbishment were executed, but major undersubscription reduced the programme from 54.76 to 23.92 crore, almost all received proceeds were deployed by June, and no room-level delivery/return milestones reconcile the spend. Disclosure contradictions further weaken reliable progress assessment.
EXEC.missing_or_limiting_evidence: Completed keys, incremental revenue, project timelines and investment recipient/outcomes.
EXEC.counterevidence: Actual share issuance, capital additions and monitored uses show activity; do not equate undersubscription alone with misconduct.
EXEC.score_basis: v 3.0 canonical factor anchors; no neutral imputation

EARN.rationale: FY26 PAT grew 19.69% but H2 turned loss-making, core room+F&B revenue declined, other operating income grew sharply and depreciation shifted materially. Current-basic proforma EPS is 0.526 versus reported FY24 EPS 1.05; issuance dilutes nominal profit recovery.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Mac Hotels is a small, concentrated Goa hotel/property turnaround and capital-allocation situation, not a demonstrated compounder. There is a real operating hotel, historical property ownership and reported positive FY2026 profit. The decisive weakness is not merely a high quoted multiple: the full audit package contains material unresolved contradictions, cash realization is persistently weak, and newly raised cash has largely been deployed while future warrant exercise remains optional. At the stale secondary ₹75.90 observation, no ordinary return, entry range or favorable investment classification is defensible. Classification: Hold — unresolved / insufficient funded and trading evidence. An auditor-reconciled filing, current conservative funding bridge and room-level returns on the new money would be more important than a lower price alone.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Exact legal/security identity: Mac Hotels Limited; CIN L55101GA1990PLC001100; BSE 541973; ISIN INE004Z01011. The official 19 October master carries MACH$ and SM/ST reference rows, lot 1500 and 6,356,421 issued shares. It is not proof of an NSE listing. Financial scope is the listed standalone entity; group-branded hotels are not automatically in this perimeter. The report cutoff is 20 October 2026, intended price reference 19 October, with only a stale 14 October secondary ₹75.90 observation available. Horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031 and hurdle 15% nominal pretax equity CAGR; ₹5 lakh is only an illustrative position. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Hold-unverified and G4 Hold-incomplete. Confidence is high on what the retrieved filings actually state, medium on historical economic comparability, and low on current project returns, cash feasibility and execution liquidity. The annual report claims Ind AS while the half-year note invokes SME exemption, so accounting basis is explicitly unresolved rather than silently chosen.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV 1, DUR 4, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 4 and EARN 4. IAS R/D/P/L are NS. BQS known weighted contribution is 2.68 with 88% original-weight coverage and mathematical missing-factor bounds 2.80–3.88. GQS known contribution is 2.00 with 85% coverage and bounds 2.15–3.50. IAS has 0% computable original-weight coverage because BQS and all investment-specific inputs are NS. Bounds are not scores or rankings; no coverage reweighting or neutral 5 is used. Persistent CASH 2 invokes a GQS ceiling 5 only if otherwise scoreable; it does not convert NS to 5. GOV 4 does not invoke the severe governance cap. G2 independently forbids a favorable investment classification. All three ranking eligibilities are false. Exact Decimal weights, individual contributions, counterevidence and missing facts are embedded in the canonical audit.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The FY2026 MD&A identifies one operating Resort Park Avenue in Goa. The 2018 prospectus described 50 guest rooms over 3,225 square metres and a management-services agreement with Alcott/OYO. That is historical context, not proof of 2026 capacity, current distribution terms or occupancy. Rooms contribute ₹2.785 crore, food/beverage ₹0.407 crore and other operating income ₹1.385 crore in FY2026. Accommodation, room-management purchase, rent and royalty expenses must be considered together: note 30 rent is ₹0.266 crore, room-management purchase ₹0.399 crore and related royalty ₹0.036 crore. Some land/flats are owned and other room premises historically leased from related entities, with historical leases expiring in 2020; renewal, title and effective operating rights are not inferred. Current room count, occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, direct-versus-OTA mix, seasonality and customer concentration remain undisclosed in the retrieved current filings. Inventory is overwhelmingly linen/crockery rather than food inputs, so manufacturing-style inventory turnover or COGS payable days would be misleading.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text: A single resort has exposure to the local destination, seasonality, distribution intermediaries and nearby alternatives. Owned property offers a location base but is not itself proof of high incremental return or a branded distribution moat. Primary peer disclosures are used as operating context, not valuation shortcuts. Grand Continent FY2026 India reported 68% occupancy and ₹3,968 ARR, but leisure occupancy was 45% and unit EBITDA 8%, versus stronger mature business properties. Its overall adjusted EBITDA ₹27.96 crore on ₹140.53 crore operating revenue also differs from unit-level metrics. Kamat Q1 FY2027 reported 66% occupancy, ₹5,678 ARR and 27% EBITDA margin across a much larger estate. Lemon Tree Q3 FY2026 reported 73.4% occupancy, ₹7,487 ARR and 50.6% net EBITDA margin, with major brand, scale, ownership and lease-accounting differences. Mac has no disclosed comparable current KPI set. Hence peers bound scenario plausibility but neither their premium multiples nor their margins are mechanically transferred.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text: Reported revenue was ₹6.793 crore in FY2019, ₹8.320 crore in FY2020, ₹1.960 crore in the FY2021 pandemic trough, ₹3.269 crore in FY2022, ₹5.384 crore in FY2023, ₹5.968 crore in FY2024, ₹3.717 crore in FY2025 and ₹4.577 crore in FY2026. The full historical table retains yearly rupee additions and growth. To avoid a closure-base illusion, the selected scoring window is the three-year FY23–FY26 CAGR of -5.27%; the five-year FY21–FY26 figure of 18.48% and six-year pre-pandemic context of -9.48% are shown, not hidden. FY2026 room revenue rose 14.48%, F&B fell 49.94%, and other operating income rose 197.96%. Room plus F&B therefore fell 1.67%, while poorly explained other operating income generated the headline 23.16% total increase. No separate organic/acquisition or room-volume/yield bridge is established. REV starts at 1 for negative comparable growth, with no trajectory adjustment. H1 profit is not annualized because full-year results imply an H2 loss.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: New rooms/refurbishment could raise occupancy and realized room rates, but spend is not a return. FY2026 cash capex was ₹5.253 crore, including substantial furniture and premises additions, while security deposits grew ₹2.389 crore. The June 2026 monitoring report records ₹8.34 crore deployed from the new issue, of which ₹3.81 crore combined working capital/construction/renovation, ₹1.35 crore land, ₹3.00 crore strategic investment and ₹0.18 crore general purposes. The recipient and operating economics of the strategic investment are not established; proposed expanded business objects are not forecast revenue. Current ROCE and a rough FY24–FY26 incremental NOPAT/capital proxy are disclosed only as diagnostics because maintenance/expansion allocation, project commissioning, deposit recoverability and income comparability are unresolved. CAP remains NS rather than automatically low. A defensible scaling plan needs keys×available nights×occupancy×ADR, ancillary contribution, recurring rent/management cost, maintenance capex, taxes and all project capital. The scenario model includes these mechanics without pretending the missing KPIs were observed.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text: Edwin Cotta and Edgar Cotta lead the company; Hotel Miramar Comfort Private Limited is a corporate promoter and related counterparty. Stewardship questions focus on capital allocation and disclosure reliability, not unsupported allegations. Directors’ remuneration ₹0.24 crore equals about 72% of FY2026 PAT; the auditor first states non-compliance with the maximum-remuneration provisions and then states compliance. Related deposit additions and the ₹8.5 crore related-party land proposal are material against the existing hotel business. EGM materials cite approvals and an external valuation, but the valuation/title evidence was not retrieved, so neither fair value nor abuse is concluded. AOC-2 room-management purchase ₹0.399 crore versus RPT-note service purchase ₹0.380 crore needs reconciliation. Execution is mixed: the FY2025 issue raised ₹11.0514 crore; the later proposed ₹54.76 crore programme was undersubscribed and revised to ₹23.92 crore. Received June 2026 cash was approximately ₹8.429 crore, nearly all deployed, while disclosed room-level delivery and capital-return milestones are absent. The 1 September price-query reply expressly says required disclosures were made and no price-sensitive announcement was pending; this response is preserved rather than portraying an unanswered exchange query.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: The full statutory package, not just the clean opinion, was inspected. Main and IFC opinions are unmodified; database-layer audit-trail coverage was not enabled and third-party coverage was unavailable, while tested application logs showed no tampering. CARO describes no immovable/tangible/intangible assets despite ₹9.733 crore PPE, and no term-loan borrowing despite long-term bank debt rising sharply. It reports inadequate inventory-verification procedures while saying no material discrepancy was noticed. It repeats the prior-year share issuance and contains conflicting remuneration and statutory-dues statements. These are material unresolved reliability issues, not proven fraud. FY2026 EBITDA ₹2.161 crore is not cash: pre-working-capital operating cash ₹2.071 crore becomes CFO-₹3.620 crore after ₹5.692 crore absorption, including deposits/advances and payable runoff. FY24–26 cumulative PAT ₹0.929 crore compares with CFO ₹-6.163 crore and FCF ₹-12.842 crore. Reclassifying debt-maturity flows and adding back related deposit increases still leaves FY25/FY26 CFO about -₹0.945/-₹1.064 crore. Receivables 44.84% older than one year and doubtful/disputed balances 34.61% require collection/allowance evidence. March gross debt ₹5.145 crore includes ₹0.248 crore current maturities exactly once; disclosed 1–5 year maturities ₹1.366 crore and >5 year ₹3.531 crore are not all assumed due within the investment horizon. Gratuity/leave expense is nil but obligations are not assumed zero. All historical financial rows and derived ratios are embedded.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text: The stale ₹75.90 reference and current 6.356421 m shares imply ₹48.245 crore market cap and 144.4 times FY2026 PAT, not a live executable valuation. Using March debt/cash yields an indicative historical EV/EBITDA of 24.5 times; it is not silently treated as October EV. The earnings method values operating land/rooms in EV and adds no separate operating property NAV. A separate March asset-haircut stress is mutually exclusive, with no independent appraisal or price target. Forecasts use historical 50 keys only as an assumption: bear/base/bull starting occupancy 40/55/65%, ADR ₹2500/3300/4000 and post-rent EBITDA 12/30/38%, with maintenance 12/10/8% of revenue and exit EV/EBITDA 6/8/10. Current funded feasibility is unverified, so ordinary returns, base targets and 12/15/18% hurdle entry prices remain null, even when algebraic terminal values are positive. Annual tables show cash, interest, principal, programme use, operating reserves and dilution. Optional warrant proceeds ₹15.498 crore and 4.591903 m new shares enter together; deposits already received are never counted again. Hypothetical rescues show fees/gross/net/share issuance and holder dilution separately, with no claim of availability. Reverse expectations return no feasible funded bracket, not a search endpoint. Sensitivities test cash floors, ADR, maintenance, working capital, rates, rent, obligations, deferral, overruns and exit multiples. A precise terminal-value-dominated DCF is not forced on unresolved hotel/property economics.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The linked failure path is a low-occupancy/yield resort that cannot turn reported other revenue into cash, while maintenance, rent and debt service continue. Related deposits/old receivables may realize slowly; further land/strategic programme outlays can consume the cash raised. Optional warrant holders need not deliver their remaining money, particularly if the trading price falls below the ₹45 exercise price. If essential commitments cannot be deferred, outside capital may be needed and existing holders could be heavily diluted; that is a conditional loss mechanism, not an observed default. Even the illustrative full-warrant variant can encounter a programme funding gap before assumed exercise. The model separately shows a hypothetical ₹30 rescue with 2% fees, not an available offer or legally executable route. Asset recoveries are haircut alternatives, not guaranteed collateral or additions to earnings EV. The strongest countercase is that refurbishment and land are legitimately value-accretive, deposits are recoverable and current liquidity is stronger than old disclosures show. That case must be substantiated with reconciled published accounts, project returns and funded obligations rather than optimistic NAV or optional money.

sections.title: Fivefold and Tenfold Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold shareholder value in five years require about 37.97% and 58.49% CAGR respectively. On unchanged current shares, the stale market-cap reference would need roughly ₹241.2 crore and ₹482.5 crore terminal equity value. At 8 times EBITDA and ignoring net debt/cash, that implies about ₹30/₹60 crore terminal EBITDA versus reported ₹2.161 crore now, before warrant or rescue dilution. No verified room count expansion, occupancy/ADR bridge, incremental-return record or funded project pipeline supports such outcomes. A high percentage rebound from the pandemic trough is not evidence of multibagger compounding. The full conversion share expansion 72.24% is not the same as existing-holder dilution 41.94%; prospective per-share gains must absorb both new capital and new shares.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Priority 1 is a reconciled auditor/issuer filing explaining the property, loan, share-issue, section 197, tax and accounting-basis contradictions; an unexplained repeat keeps G2 on Hold. Priority 2 is a published recent unrestricted-cash and debt bridge from March and June, together with essential programme commitments and deferrability, not private daily bank statements. Priority 3 is disclosure of current keys, occupancy, ADR/RevPAR and after-rent room contribution; compare these with the completed refurbishment capital. Priority 4 is cash realization: current baseline FY2026 CFO-₹3.620 crore, and still-₹1.064 crore after deposit/maturity adjustments; investigate another negative half-year or further aged-claim growth. Priority 5 is deposit and strategic-investment recoverability/recipient, land title and independent valuation. Priority 6 is warrant conversion by the disclosed 18-month window, with proceeds and dilution reconciled; optional amounts never count early. Priority 7 is debt maturities and statutory/lease obligations; any actual nonpayment or unfinanceable essential gap changes G3 from unverified to failure. Priority 8 is verified BSE 20/60 session trading, lot and restrictions before implementation. Thresholds are research alerts, not automatic trade instructions.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved, with all three aggregate scores NS and all ranking eligibilities false. The business is a turnaround/capital-allocation situation rather than a verified scalable compounder. This is not an Avoid — governance finding: GOV 4 and unresolved controls do not prove misconduct. It is also not a claimed default or suspension. The decisive needs are reliable financial statements, evidence-backed funding through essential obligations, attributable hotel/project returns and executable market data. A cheaper price would change algebraic return diagnostics but cannot by itself clear these gates. No investment, position-sizing or order-entry action is recommended by this research; the ₹5 lakh example is purely a lot/liquidity illustration. Revisit the relevant factors and gates when corrective filings and current operating/cash disclosures arrive, retaining the dated evidence and counterevidence rather than rewriting the original uncertainty.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text: Primary evidence comprises the complete FY2026 statutory report, revised FY2025 report, historical FY2020–24 reports, EGM notice, prospectus, H1 FY2026 limited-review filing, June 2026 monitoring and issuer price-query response. BSE direct attachments were denied for some items; the same issuer PDFs were obtained from the issuer or a public Business Standard filing mirror, with URLs, dates and hashes recorded. The issuer URL called Annual Report 2025 actually contains FY2025–26 and is labeled correctly in this dossier. Source retrieval after the cutoff does not admit facts published after 20 October. Peer PDFs support only operating benchmarks. Stale secondary quote/history is labeled and never silently upgraded to official liquidity. All numeric facts and explicit model assumptions are retained in source-safe extracts. Raw PDFs/OCR, images, shareholder lists, bank-account identifiers and transfer utilities are omitted from analytical backups. Reproduction checks arithmetic from retained extracts, not fresh authentication of originals. Principal open questions are current hotel keys/leases, income composition, audit corrections, deposit and investment recoverability, land value/title, current available liquidity and commitment timing, warrant conversion, and exact trading restrictions/depth. All methodology weights are research heuristics, not empirically guaranteed predictors.

evidence.claim: Exact entity is Mac Hotels Limited, CIN L55101GA1990PLC001100, BSE 541973, ISIN INE004Z01011. Official master gives 6,356,421 issued shares and lot 1,500.
evidence.locator: Cover, note 16 and exact master ISIN rows

evidence.claim: Latest FY2026 annual MD&A describes one Resort Park Avenue in Goa. The 2018 prospectus described 50 rooms and a management arrangement with Alcott/OYO; current keys, occupancy, ADR and RevPAR are not disclosed in the retrieved current reports.
evidence.locator: FY26 printed p 39; prospectus PDF pp 42,85,90–94
evidence.counterevidence: Group website hotels are not treated as assets owned by this listed entity.

evidence.claim: Selected three-year FY23–FY26 revenue CAGR is -5.27%; FY21–FY26 is +18.48% from a pandemic closure trough and is not the scoring base. FY20–FY26 CAGR is -9.48%.
evidence.locator: Historical P&L tables, model growth bridge
evidence.counterevidence: FY26 reported annual revenue grew 23.16%, but room plus F&B revenue fell 1.67%.

evidence.claim: FY26 revenue 4.577 crore includes rooms 2.785, F&B 0.407 and other operating income 1.385. Other operating income is 30.26% of total and explains the growth; composition is insufficiently disaggregated.
evidence.locator: Printed p 81, note 27
evidence.counterevidence: This is operating other income, not automatically non-operating or fictitious income.

evidence.claim: FY26 PAT 0.334 crore follows H1 PAT 0.462 crore, implying H2 loss 0.128 crore. FY26 depreciation rises from 0.272 to 1.474 crore, including 1.122 crore furniture depreciation.
evidence.locator: Annual P&L/note 6; H1 PDF p 5 image
evidence.counterevidence: Annual PAT still rose 19.69%; tax and depreciation timing need explanation before normalization.

evidence.claim: FY25/FY26 CFO was -3.745/-3.620 crore and capex 1.278/5.253 crore. After excluding current-debt-maturity movements and adding back related deposits, CFO remains approximately -0.945/-1.064 crore.
evidence.locator: Cash-flow statements and RPT note 33
evidence.counterevidence: Related deposits explain a significant portion, so all negative CFO is not attributed to lost hotel collections.

evidence.claim: Receivables of 1.213 crore include 0.138 crore doubtful and 0.282 crore disputed-good claims; 44.84% are older than one year. The face receivable note gives no allowance reconciliation.
evidence.locator: Notes 12 and 30, printed pp 74–75/82
evidence.counterevidence: Average receivable days decline approximately 84 to 79; worsening age quality is not the same as worsening aggregate DSO.

evidence.claim: Security deposits rise 2.389 crore to 5.277 crore; RPT note identifies the FY26 deposit addition to Hotel Miramar Comfort Private Limited. Related land proposal is 8.5 crore, with 1.35 crore spent by June.
evidence.locator: Notes 9/33; EGM PDF pp 29–35; monitor pp 7–9
evidence.counterevidence: Board/audit disclosures assert approvals and arm’s-length terms; no independently retrieved land valuation or title verification establishes fair value or abuse.

evidence.claim: Full FY26 audit main opinion and separate IFC opinion are unmodified, but audit-trail reporting excludes database-layer coverage and third-party controls.
evidence.locator: Printed pp 44–47 and 53–54 / PDF pp 46–49 and 55–56
evidence.counterevidence: No tampering was observed in the application logs examined; do not label this a qualified main opinion.

evidence.claim: CARO says no immovable/tangible/intangible assets despite 9.73 crore PPE and owned land/flats; says no term loan taken while long-term bank borrowing increases from 0.638 to 4.897 crore. Inventory verification is reported inappropriate.
evidence.locator: Printed pp 49–50; notes 6,17
evidence.counterevidence: CARO also says proper PPE records exist, no material inventory discrepancies noticed, no defaults or fraud reported; contradictions require reconciliation rather than fraud inference.

evidence.claim: Audit section 197 paragraphs contradict one another on maximum managerial remuneration; CARO repeats 2,631,288 shares at 42 in FY26 though this is FY25 financing. Statutory-dues descriptions and accounting basis are internally inconsistent.
evidence.locator: Printed pp 46–51; FY25 issue/cash flow; H1 note 4 and review
evidence.counterevidence: Main opinion/IFC remain unmodified; annual report says continuing auditor appointment. The contradictions are unresolved material reliability issues, not proof of intentional misconduct.

evidence.claim: At March 2026 cash is 0.467 crore and gross debt 5.145 crore, including current maturities 0.248 crore once. Bank maturity table duplicates current debt again under other financial liabilities; analytical model removes the duplicate.
evidence.locator: Notes 15,17,22,37; cash-flow classifications
evidence.counterevidence: No actual bank default or willful-defaulter status is reported.

evidence.claim: May equity cash equals 0.725133 m shares×45=3.2631 crore; warrants 4.591903 m×11.25=5.1659 crore deposit already received. Remaining warrant exercise cash 15.4977 crore is optional, not cash on hand.
evidence.locator: Monitor PDF p 5; issue detail and current master
evidence.counterevidence: Monitor rounds aggregate received to 8.44 versus 8.429 from units; 0.011 crore rounding gap retained, not silently forced.

evidence.claim: June monitoring uses 3.81+1.35+3.00+0.18=8.34 crore, leaving 15.58 crore revised programme budget to spend, not cash available. Approximately 0.0819 crore remains in named issue accounts, not verified total operating cash.
evidence.locator: PDF pp 7–9
evidence.counterevidence: Monitor reports no object deviation and no observed adverse viability event, based on supplied company/CA information; that is not proof of future funding or returns.

evidence.claim: Full warrant conversion expands shares 72.24% from current basic 6.356421 m to 10.948324 m and dilutes an existing holder 41.94%, before any rescue. FY25 issuance already diluted previous holders 46.73%.
evidence.locator: Issue arithmetic
evidence.counterevidence: Optional conversion could deliver 15.498 crore cash; both proceeds and new shares are modeled together, never one without the other.

evidence.claim: September 1 issuer reply says required disclosures were made and there was no pending undisclosed price-sensitive announcement.
evidence.locator: Complete issuer letter
evidence.counterevidence: This preserves management’s response but is not independent assurance that price movement is justified.

evidence.claim: Current incremental project returns cannot be attributed. Unadjusted FY24–FY26 incremental NOPAT/invested-capital proxy is approximately 0.98%, but deposit deployment, depreciation, project timing and income mix prevent a defensible CAP score.
evidence.locator: Historical model/capital returns, new capex and issue objects
evidence.counterevidence: Reported FY26 EBITDA 2.161 crore and positive PAT do not establish cash-on-cash returns on new money.

evidence.claim: Primary peer unit disclosures show significant differences: GCH India FY26 occupancy 68%, ARR 3968 and unit EBITDA 23%; its leisure segment 45% occupancy and 8% unit EBITDA. Kamat Q1 FY27 occupancy 66%, ARR 5678, EBITDA 27%. Lemon Tree Q3 FY26 occupancy 73.4%, ARR 7487, net EBITDA 50.6%.
evidence.locator: Issuer presentations, operating/cohort tables
evidence.counterevidence: Different mature/new, city/leisure, ownership and lease-accounting mixes mean these are scenario boundary context, not direct comparable multiples or Mac forecasts.

evidence.claim: Stale 14 October secondary price 75.90 implies current-basic market cap 48.245 crore and reported FY26 PAT multiple 144.39 x. March debt/cash EV is only a historical diagnostic, not verified current EV.
evidence.locator: Quote, official share count, reported P&L
evidence.counterevidence: No verified 19 October closing price or complete exact-session 20/60 day BSE history; failed access is missing data, not zero trading.

model_conventions.optional_exercise_date_assumption: FY2028, within the disclosed 18-month window if issued in May2026; no specific-day funding feasibility is asserted.
model_conventions.ordinary_return_gate: Current funding/capital feasibility is not verified. All ordinary returns and investable entry prices are null. Rescue and algebraic diagnostics are not executable recommendations.
model_conventions.programme_timing: Remaining June programme expenditure is assumed 75% during post-entry FY27 and 25% in FY28. This is a cash stress schedule, not a verified commitment calendar. Optional warrants assumed exercised in FY28; their actual timing and participation are unknown.
model_conventions.cash_overlap_control: The observed June 8.34 crore programme uses are charged once. Pre-entry recurring operating cash is modeled only July 1 to October 20 to avoid charging the April–June mixed working-capital/construction use again. Principal/interest are modeled separately April–October, so an overlap bound is also disclosed.
model_conventions.lease_treatment: Model EBITDA is after ordinary rent, room-management and royalty expense. No lease liability is added on top absent a verified obligation schedule. Rent escalations and an unquantified-obligation reserve are separately stressed.
model_conventions.property_treatment: Operating land, premises and rooms are in the earnings enterprise value, never added again. New land and strategic investment recoveries are zero in the default terminal value; a separate asset haircut check is not added to EV.
model_conventions.programme_overlap_bound: June programme uses include mixed construction, working capital and general purposes. Some rent/interest/principal or recurring cost could overlap with these uses; this cannot be quantified. Deferral and lower-use stress variants show the sensitivity, but none verifies funding.
model_conventions.maturity_tail: The over-five-year March2026 bucket may include obligations between April and October2031. Base assumes none due in the terminal stub only as an explicit sensitivity convention; a full3.5307288crore pre-terminal balloon stress is also modeled. Exact dates are not disclosed.

Optional warrant/rescue dilution raises aggregate requirements further. No attributable room, capital or funding bridge supports these outcomes.

limitations: Forecasts are explicit scenario assumptions, not guidance. Historical 50 keys do not verify current room count.
Ordinary entry prices and returns remain null in every scenario because current funding feasibility is unverified.
Actual financial reliability and tradability are independently unresolved; even a modeled cash-floor pass would not clear those gates.

No DCF is forced: weak project/unit disclosures, a finite mixed property/lease estate and unresolved cash normalization make a precise terminal-value-dominated DCF misleading. EV/after-rent EBITDA, normalized earnings and non-additive asset stresses are retained.

summary: Mac Hotels is a small, concentrated Goa hotel/property turnaround and capital-allocation situation, not a demonstrated compounder. There is a real operating hotel, historical property ownership and reported positive FY2026 profit. The decisive weakness is not merely a high quoted multiple: the full audit package contains material unresolved contradictions, cash realization is persistently weak, and newly raised cash has largely been deployed while future warrant exercise remains optional. At the stale secondary ₹75.90 observation, no ordinary return, entry range or favorable investment classification is defensible. Classification: Hold — unresolved / insufficient funded and trading evidence. An auditor-reconciled filing, current conservative funding bridge and room-level returns on the new money would be more important than a lower price alone.
